anchor.quote: Here $\kappa$ denotes the real number being rounded up, such as $2.3$ or $-1.5$.
The **ceiling** of $\kappa$, written $\lceil \kappa \rceil$, is the least integer that is not less than $\kappa$.
An integer is its own ceiling, so $\lceil k \rceil = k$ whenever $k$ is an integer.
anchor.note: The page says k is an integer, but not what k counts or denotes. The only earlier binding of k, the cofactor on prime-number, is not the meaning used here.
